title: Paying wages
hook: pay the worker before his sweat dries (Ibn Majah)
tomorrow: someone owes you money and can't pay. now what?

segments.voice: Yesterday, honest dealing: the wet grain belongs on top. Nothing hidden. Today, the money goes the other way, from the one who hires to the one who works.

An invoice that says net thirty. A babysitter waiting by the door while the parents dig for cash. A first paycheck that arrives a week late, with a sorry email. So when exactly is pay owed? A hadith in Ibn Majah gives an answer you can feel on your skin: give the worker his wages before his sweat dries.
screen: `NET THIRTY. A WEEK LATE.` → `WHEN IS PAY OWED?` → `BEFORE HIS SWEAT DRIES.`

segments.voice: Muslims read that line in more than one way, and both readings have a case. The first stays close to the picture. Sweat dries fast. Work done today is paid today, especially for the day laborer who needs it for dinner. Every hour you hold it, you're holding something that isn't yours. The second reading hears it as a picture of promptness. Pay can come weekly or monthly, if that's what both sides agreed; what the saying forbids is dragging past the day it's due. A business with a payroll date isn't breaking the hadith, so long as the date is kept. Some scholars also note the line's chain is debated on its own, and lean on other reports beside it. And here is where the two agree, in a report in Sahih al-Bukhari. God says there are three whom He will oppose on the Day of Resurrection, and one is a man who hires a worker, takes the full work from him, and doesn't pay his wage. So the question isn't really weekly or daily. It's whether the worker has to chase what he's already earned. One to tell a friend: in that hadith, God Himself takes the unpaid worker's side.
screen: `READING ONE: PAY IT TODAY.` · `READING TWO: PAY IT WHEN DUE.` · `BOTH: NEVER HOLD IT BACK.` · `GOD TAKES THE WORKER'S SIDE.` · then, large: `BEFORE THE SWEAT DRIES.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind anyone you owe right now: a friend who covered lunch, a sitter, a coworker who chipped in for a gift. Send it now, or write down the exact day you will. Then sit for the rest of the time with nothing owed left floating.
screen: `WHO DO YOU OWE?` · `SEND IT, OR SET THE DAY.`

segments.voice: Paying wages: giving a worker what they've earned, on time, without making them chase it. Before the sweat dries.
Hold on to this: before the sweat dries, the pay is theirs. Three of ten, done.

howItsDone: Muslim employers are taught to pay wages in full and on time, whether by the day or on an agreed schedule; withholding a worker's earned pay is counted a serious wrong.

match.prompt: the saying and the readings — tap the pairs.

myth: in a report in Bukhari, God opposes one who hires a worker and withholds his wage
he takes the full work and doesn't pay: one of three God will oppose.
Muslims all agree the saying means pay within the hour
some read it close to the letter; others as 'on the agreed day'. both forbid holding back what's due.

fork.setup: your aunt hires a neighbor's teenager to rake leaves on Saturday, then says she'll pay with the family bills at month's end. they never agreed on that. what fits?
options: month's end is fine; the one paying decides when pay is due.
pay when the job is done, or on a day they both agree to first.
pay half now and half later, so everyone shares the wait.
fork.reveal: both readings meet here: pay on completion, or on the day agreed. what neither allows is the worker waiting on terms they never accepted.

original.note: Arabic: a wage, the pay for work done.

trapdoor: what you thought: pay is due whenever the boss gets to it.
what it means: a worker's earned pay is theirs; paying it late, or making them chase it, is a wrong.
what a scholar hears: Ibn Majah 2443, 'before his sweat dries' (its chain discussed, supported by other reports); Bukhari 2227, the hadith qudsi of the three God will oppose.
guess: giving workers their earned pay on time, in full
paying workers only when the business is doing well
tipping a server on top of the price of a meal

chat.says: Jordan worked her first saturday 🙌 dad's tight on cash, wants to pay her a week late. one week?
options: Pay her on the due date. Holding back earned pay is what the hadith warns about.
A week is fine if you explain it; she's a friend, so the rule is looser.
Late is fine as long as you add a little extra to make up for the wait.
chat.meaning: Readings differ on daily or agreed pay, but both forbid holding back a wage once it's due. In Bukhari, God opposes the one who withholds it.

Ibn Majah.meaning: a classic collection of hadith, named for its compiler

Sahih al-Bukhari.meaning: a major collection of reports of the Prophet's words and deeds

Day of Resurrection.meaning: the Day of Judgment, when all are raised

sources.ref: Sunan Ibn Majah 2443 (give the worker his wages before his sweat dries)
Sahih al-Bukhari 2227 (hadith qudsi: three whom God will oppose, including one who hires a worker, takes full work and doesn't pay him)
